What is the Optimal Stopping Theorem 2?
customset-mv7yibh6-dl43np.back:
Let $(M_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be martingale process and let $T$ be a finite-valued stopping time. If $\exist C < \infty$ such that one of the two hold: $\\$
a) $|M_n| \le C \quad \forall n \le T \\$
b) $\mathbb{E}(T) < \infty$ and $|M_n - M_{n-1}| \le C \quad \forall n \le T \\$
Then, $\mathbb{E}(M_T) = \mathbb{E}(M_0)$

Prove Optimal Stopping Theorem 2: $\\$
Let $(M_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be martingale process and let $T$ be a finite-valued stopping time. If $\exist C < \infty$ such that one of the two hold: $\\$
a) ...$\\$

Then, ...
customset-mv7yibh6-dl43np.back:
Define $T_n = min(T,n)$ so $T_n$ is a bounded stopping time. Since $T$ is finite, $T = T_n$ eventually so $M_{T_n} \to M_T$ as $n \to \infty$ and by Optimal Stopping Theorem 1, $\mathbb{E}(M_{T_n}) = \mathbb{E}(M_0) \\$  If (a) $|M_n| \le C \: \forall n \le T $ holds then $\sup_{n} |M_{T_n}| \le C$ so $\mathbb{E}(M_{T_n}) \to \mathbb{E}(M_T)$ by bounded convergence. $\\$
If (b) $\mathbb{E}(T) < \infty$ and $|M_n - M_{n-1}| \le C \: \forall n \le T$ holds then $\sup_n |M_{T_n}| \le CT + M_0$ and by dominated convergence $\mathbb{E}(M_{T_n}) \to \mathbb{E}(M_T) \\$
Then letting $n \to \infty$, $\mathbb{E}(M_T) = \mathbb{E}(M_0)$

customset-mv7yibh6-dl43np.front: What is the tower property? Prove it.
customset-mv7yibh6-dl43np.back:
If $H \subseteq G$ is a $\sigma$-algebra. Then $\mathbb{E}(\mathbb{E}(X|G)|H) = \mathbb{E}(X|H) \\$
Let $Y = \mathbb{E}(\mathbb{E}(X|G)|H)$ almost surely then if $A \in H \implies A \in G$ so 
$$ \mathbb{E}(Y 1_A) = \mathbb{E}(\mathbb{E}(X|G)1_A) = \mathbb{E}(X 1_A)$$
Since Y is integrable and $H$-measurable, $Y = \mathbb{E}(X|H)$ almost surely
